parsed.explanation: The combined regime stacks a national document/entry regime — X markers barred, officers instructed to refuse on any document discrepancy casting doubt on sex, possible lifetime fraud finding, travelers stranded — onto division-level exposures. Universal facility-by-birth-sex exposure exists across ~19 states (criminal in 4), with a documented trespass arrest and a 60-day penalty. In this division a mob beat a trans couple; the victims were charged, no attacker arrested, one denied hospital care and jailed/searched in a men's facility despite a female marker. Federal immigration custody documents beatings, sexual abuse and forced labour, and 2026 conversion-therapy mandates for federal prisoners. Protections (national hate-crime and employment law, enjoinments, litigation) operate partially but do not reach these exposures.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 cable directs refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex; X/diverse markers barred for new issues; possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; trans travelers report confiscated/blocked passports and being stranded abroad; 8+ foreign governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid to expiry; ACLU suit pending; legal-aid FAQ on document rules; entry refusal is administrative, not criminal, and fraud finding is never automatic.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy → refusal/secondary screening → immigration custody, where documented trans-inmate abuse and birth-sex placement apply.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented trespass arrest (up to 60 days) under a bathroom law; victim held 24h in men's ward and searched by male guard despite female marker; federal corrections conversion-therapy mandates (hair, hormones, drugs) from 2026; immigration custody reports beatings, solitary, forced labour and severe sexual abuse of trans detainees.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Some executive orders enjoined; national hate-crime statute reaches bias violence; counsel/advocates litigate arrests.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Federal redefinition of sex at birth overrides division document markers in custody, so a female-marked licence does not protect housing or search.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Bans on identity-congruent facility use in ~19 state/provinces (9+1 all government buildings, 9 schools-plus, 3 schools-only); criminal offence in 4; at least one severe municipal ordinance passed alongside a mob attack; map notes other sex-defining laws may still apply elsewhere.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 state/provinces, 4 units and the capital district have no mapped ban; most bans cover government-owned settings only; national funding orders driving bans are partly litigated.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal funding and 'sex' redefinition push state bans; trespass statutes convert a universal facility exposure into arrest risk.

care_services.exposure: Division banned minors' gender-affirming care (in force 2024); 27 states ban such care; one mob-attack victim was denied hospital care and taken to jail; executive order frames care as 'mutilation'; Oct 2025 proposed rule would bar public-insurance reimbursement for under-18 trans patients.
care_services.protection: National employment nondiscrimination (2020) and marriage/adoption equality stand; adult emergency care denial documented only in the attack victim case, not as a general rule; several orders blocked in court.
care_services.interaction: Care denial at intake → custody transfer into men's facility; minor in a travelling family could face division care ban if treatment is needed.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders label care 'mutilation' and direct investigation of 'gender ideology'; Dec 2025 reward memo uses 'radical gender ideology' among extremist animating viewpoints; May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritizes neutralizing groups 'radically pro-transgender'; 'forbidden terms' purge of gender/LGBT content.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: The reward memo states the phrase is not a reward criterion, and the strategy says counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; several orders enjoined.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing plausibly lowers the threshold for aggressive enforcement and raises street-level hostility toward outed visitors.

minors_guardians.exposure: Facility bans cover K-12 schools; Jan 2025 order directs criminal investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition; minors' care banned in the division and 27 states nationally.
minors_guardians.protection: Marriage equality and joint adoption rights recognized in the division; no documented visitor-facing family-custody seizure rule.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor in a travelling family shares facility and emergency-care exposure; parent's trans status plus a care-seeking event could trigger scrutiny, but this pathway is not documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Aug 2026 mob beat a trans couple over restroom use; both victims charged with disturbing the peace, no attacker arrested, one denied care and jailed in men's facility; a trans inmate killed in a division prison (Apr 2024); division reported highest per-capita trans-women killing rate (figure is an undercount floor, so magnitude unusable).
street_violence_police_response.protection: National 2009 hate-crime statute covers gender identity (division's 1997 statute does not); municipal non-discrimination ordinances in two municipalities.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Victims-charged/no-attacker-arrested outcome shows state response as bystandly or hostile, reducing reliance on hate-crime recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit, executive-order challenges and proposed health rules all unresolved, so exposure shifts with injunctions; division has no state gender-identity discrimination law and sits in the index's lowest band; which orders are in force at travel time is uncertain.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have blocked or enjoined several measures; ACLU litigation, legal-aid FAQ, equality/identity-document maps, and national employment and hate-crime law provide partial, functioning recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedy timelines (months of litigation) exceed a visitor's stay, so paper recourse rarely reaches an incident in real time.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like 0.35-A, refusal is instructed where sex is in doubt and there is no real-time appeal — a universal entry exposure. But the consequences are administrative refusal rather than a permanent conduct register, existing X passports remain valid, litigation is live, and no agency-controlled appeals-only remedy is documented; therefore materially above 0.35-A.

0.55-B offers discretionary secondary screening, administrative refusal and slow appeals with no custody. This dossier adds a documented arrest with jail exposure, birth-sex custody placement with male search, denied hospital care, impunity for a mob attack, and documented abuse in immigration custody — heavier severity and state involvement, so below 0.55-B.

0.75-C features trained officers, brief detention ending in release, written reasons, counsel access and compensation. Here entry refusal carries a possible lifetime fraud finding, custody placement is by birth sex with documented harm, and remedies are unresolved litigation rather than an operative tribunal — clearly below 0.75-C.

Closest match: routine universal exposure at checkpoints/services, detention and humiliation, denial of care, scarce legal aid, inconsistent enforcement and no credible execution. This dossier sits just below it because imprisonment is an actual documented outcome (trespass arrest, men's-ward custody) and state failure to act against violence is documented.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces a two-level system. Nationally, documents are the chokepoint: marker rules, a cable instructing refusal on any sex-related discrepancy, and a possible lifetime fraud finding reach every trans visitor, with litigation unresolved and remedies measured in months. Facility bans and trespass arrest convert everyday use of public buildings into criminal exposure in a minority of states, including this division. Here the operative regime is worst: birth-sex custody placement overrides a female-marked licence, hospital care was denied, and victims were charged while no attacker was arrested — state response as bystander. Immigration-custody abuse and 2026 conversion-therapy mandates add state-perpetrated severity for anyone detained. National hate-crime and employment law, enjoinments and active litigation partially offset but do not reach these exposures, placing the combined regime at the low end of Elevated Risk.
